resposta:
**Secretários de Estado dos EUA (início de 2018 até o fim de 2024)**  
*(incluindo secretários interinos/atuais)*  

| Período | Nome | Partido | Função / Observação |
|---------|------|---------|----------------------|
| **Feb 1 2017 – Mar 31 2018** | **Rex Tillerson** | Republicano | Secretário de Estado (entregou em Mar 31 2018) |
| **Abr 1 2018 – Abr 26 2018** | **John J. Sullivan** | Republicano | *Secretário em exercício* (interino) – nomeado por Trump para cobrir a transição |
| **Abr 26 2018 – Jan 20 2021** | **Michael R. Pompeo** | Republicano | Secretário de Estado (full‑term) |
| **Jan 20 2021 – Jan 26 2021** | **Stephen E. Biegun** | Republicano | *Secretário em exercício* (interino) – designado como vice‑secretário e atuou enquanto Biden assumia o cargo |
| **Jan 26 2021 – Apr 14 2021** | **Daniel Bennett Smith** | Independente | *Secretário em exercício* (interino) – nomeado após a confirmação de Blinken |
| **Jan 26 2021 – Presente (até 31 déc 2024)** | **Antony J. Blinken** | Democrata | Secretário de Estado (full‑term) |

### Detalhes importantes

- **Rex Tillerson** foi o último do administration de Trump antes da mudança de governo.
- **John J. Sullivan** serviu apenas alguns dias como secretário em exercício entre Tillerson e Pompeo.
- **Mike Pompeo** assumiu formalmente em 26 abril 2018 e permaneceu até a posse de Joe Biden.
- **Stephen Biegun** foi nomeado vice‑secretário e, em 20 de jan 2021, tornou-se *acting secretary* temporariamente enquanto Biden tomava posse.
- **Daniel Bennett Smith** foi nomeado *acting secretary* logo após a confirmação de Blinken (26 jan 2021) e atuou até 14 abr 2021, quando Wendy Sherman assumiu como vice‑secretário.
- **Antony Blinken** foi confirmado pelo Senado em 26 jan 2021 e juramentado na mesma data, permanecendo no cargo até pelo menos 31 dez 2024 (e além).

Esses são todos os ocupantes que governaram o cargo de Secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos desde o início de 2018 até o final de 2024, incluindo todas as funções interinas ou atuais.

This is a **list of United States secretaries of state**.

## Secretaries of foreign affairs (1781–1789)

On January 10, 1780, the [Congress of the Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Confederation "Congress of the Confederation") created the Department of Foreign Affairs.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_secretaries_of_state#cite_note-1)

On August 10, 1781, Congress selected [Robert R. Livingston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_R._Livingston "Robert R. Livingston"), a delegate from [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)"), as the first secretary for foreign affairs. Livingston was unable to take office until October 20, 1781. He served until June 4, 1783, and was succeeded by [Elias Boudinot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Boudinot "Elias Boudinot"), who was succeeded by [John Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jay "John Jay") on December 21, 1784, who served until March 4, 1789, when the government under the [Articles of Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Articles_of_Confederation "Articles of Confederation") gave way to the government under the [Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States").

The office of secretary of foreign affairs and the Department of Foreign Affairs were reinstated by a law signed by [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington") on July 27, 1789. [John Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jay "John Jay") retained the post on an interim basis, pending the return of [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") from France.

## Secretaries of state

On September 15, 1789, before Jefferson could return to take the post, Washington signed into law another act which changed the name of the office from Secretary of Foreign Affairs to [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State"), changed the name of the department to the [Department of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State"), and added several domestic powers and responsibilities to both the office of secretary and the department. [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") took office as the first secretary of state on March 22, 1790.

This is a list of United States secretaries of state by time in office. This is based on the difference between dates; if counted by number of calendar days all the figures would be one greater. [Cordell Hull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cordell_Hull "Cordell Hull") is the only person to have served as secretary of state for more than eight years. [Daniel Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Webster "Daniel Webster") and [James G. Blaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_G._Blaine "James G. Blaine") are the only secretaries of state to have ever served non-consecutive terms. [Warren Christopher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Christopher "Warren Christopher") served very briefly as acting secretary of state non-consecutively with his later tenure as full-fledged secretary of state. [Elihu B. Washburne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elihu_B._Washburne "Elihu B. Washburne") served as secretary of state for less than two weeks before becoming [ambassador to France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_France "List of ambassadors of the United States to France").

**Daniel Bennett Smith** (born March 6, 1956) is an American diplomat who served as the director of the [Foreign Service Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Service_Institute "Foreign Service Institute") and acting [United States Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State") at the [presidential transition of Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_transition_of_Joe_Biden "Presidential transition of Joe Biden").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-1) He has held the rank of [career ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_Foreign_Service_Career_Ambassadors "List of United States Foreign Service Career Ambassadors") since September 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-Training-2) He previously served as [Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_Secretary_of_State_for_Intelligence_and_Research "Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research") at the [United States Department of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State"), assuming that post on February 14, 2014.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-DOSBIO-3) He is considered a veteran diplomat by the U.S. diplomatic community.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-4)

## Early life and education

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Ambassador_Smith_Gives_Remarks_at_his_Swearing-in_Ceremony_%2845570913001%29.jpg/250px-Ambassador_Smith_Gives_Remarks_at_his_Swearing-in_Ceremony_%2845570913001%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ambassador_Smith_Gives_Remarks_at_his_Swearing-in_Ceremony_(45570913001).jpg)Smith delivers remarks at his swearing-in ceremony at the [Foreign Service Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Service_Institute "Foreign Service Institute") at the [George P. Shultz National Foreign Affairs Training Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Foreign_Affairs_Training_Center "National Foreign Affairs Training Center") in [Arlington, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington_County,_Virginia "Arlington County, Virginia") on October 26, 2018.

Smith obtained a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") degree in history from the [University of Colorado Boulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Colorado_Boulder "University of Colorado Boulder"), followed by a Master of Arts and PhD from [Stanford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_University "Stanford University").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-DOSBIO-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-5) His dissertation is titled "Toward Internationalism: [New Deal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal "New Deal") Foreign Economic Policy, 1933–39", and was completed in 1983.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-6)

## Career

Under President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"), Smith served as the [United States Ambassador to Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Ambassador_to_Greece "United States Ambassador to Greece") from 2010 to 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-7)

In 2018, Smith was selected to serve as the Director of the Foreign Service Institute.

In 2021, President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") selected Smith to serve as the acting secretary of state until his nominee for the position, [Antony Blinken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken "Antony Blinken"), was confirmed by the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-8) Blinken was confirmed on January 26, 2021.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Bennett_Smith#cite_note-9) On May 3, 2021, Smith was appointed as US envoy to India.

**Stephen Edward Biegun**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Biegun#cite_note-1) (born March 30, 1963) is an American businessman and diplomat who served as the [United States deputy secretary of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_State "United States Deputy Secretary of State") from December 2019 to January 2021 and [United States Special Representative for North Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Special_Representative_for_North_Korea "United States Special Representative for North Korea") from August 2018 to January 2021,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Biegun#cite_note-2) vice president of international governmental affairs for the [Ford Motor Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company "Ford Motor Company"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Biegun#cite_note-3) staffer on the [National Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Security_Council "United States National Security Council"), as well as national security adviser to Senator [Bill Frist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Frist "Bill Frist").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Biegun#cite_note-4)

## Early life and education

Stephen Edward Biegun was born in [Detroit, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit,_Michigan "Detroit, Michigan"). He earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Russian and political science from the [University of Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan "University of Michigan") in 1984.

## Career

He was the in-country director for the [International Republican Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Republican_Institute "International Republican Institute") in Moscow, Russia, from 1992 to 1994. He was a member of the board of the [U.S. Russia Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Russia_Foundation "U.S. Russia Foundation"), the Moscow School of Political Studies, the [U.S.–Russia Business Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S.–Russia_Business_Council "U.S.–Russia Business Council"), the [National Bureau of Asian Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Asian_Research "National Bureau of Asian Research"), the [U.S.-ASEAN Business Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S.-ASEAN_Business_Council?action=edit&redlink=1 "U.S.-ASEAN Business Council (page does not exist)"), and [Freedom House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_House "Freedom House").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Biegun#cite_note-5)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Secretary_Pompeo_Swears_in_Stephen_E._Biegun_as_Deputy_Secretary_of_State_%2849252860693%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Pompeo_Swears_in_Stephen_E._Biegun_as_Deputy_Secretary_of_State_%2849252860693%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Pompeo_Swears_in_Stephen_E._Biegun_as_Deputy_Secretary_of_State_(49252860693).jpg)Biegun is sworn in by [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State") [Mike Pompeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo "Mike Pompeo") to serve as [Deputy Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_State "United States Deputy Secretary of State") at the [U.S. Department of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State") on December 21, 2019.

Biegun has held a number of offices within the federal government, including executive secretary of the [National Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Security_Council "United States National Security Council"), reporting to national security adviser [Condoleezza Rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condoleezza_Rice "Condoleezza Rice") under President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush"). He was a foreign policy adviser to [Sarah Palin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Palin "Sarah Palin") during [John McCain's 2008 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain_2008_presidential_campaign "John McCain 2008 presidential campaign").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Biegun#cite_note-6) On March 1, 2018, it was reported that Biegun was a top candidate to replace [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s national security adviser [H. R. McMaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._R._McMaster "H. R. McMaster").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Biegun#cite_note-7) On March 22, it was announced that McMaster would instead be succeeded by [John Bolton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bolton "John Bolton").

On August 23, 2018, [U.S. Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State") [Mike Pompeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pompeo "Mike Pompeo") appointed Biegun as the [U.S. special representative for North Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Special_Representative_for_North_Korea "United States Special Representative for North Korea"), directing policy in regard to [North Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea "North Korea") on behalf of the [Trump administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "First presidency of Donald Trump").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Biegun#cite_note-8)

On August 7, 2019, *[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")* reported that Biegun was a top candidate to replace [Jon Huntsman Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Huntsman_Jr. "Jon Huntsman Jr.") as [United States ambassador to Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Ambassador_to_Russia "United States Ambassador to Russia"). After [John Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_J._Sullivan_(diplomat) "John J. Sullivan (diplomat)") was instead nominated, Biegun was nominated to replace him as [deputy secretary of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_State "United States Deputy Secretary of State") on October 31, 2019. His nomination was confirmed by a 90–3 vote of the [U.S. Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") on December 19, 2019.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Biegun#cite_note-9) He was sworn in two days later.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Biegun#cite_note-10)

**Antony John Blinken** (born April 16, 1962) is an American lawyer and diplomat who served as the 71st [United States secretary of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_secretary_of_state "United States secretary of state") from 2021 to 2025. He previously served as [deputy national security advisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_National_Security_Advisor "Deputy National Security Advisor") from 2013 to 2015 and [deputy secretary of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Secretary_of_State "Deputy Secretary of State") from 2015 to 2017 under President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-auto-1) Blinken was previously [national security advisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Advisor_to_the_Vice_President "National Security Advisor to the Vice President") to then-vice president [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") from 2009 to 2013.

During the [Clinton administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Bill_Clinton "Presidency of Bill Clinton"), Blinken served in the [State Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State") and in senior positions on the [National Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Security_Council "United States National Security Council") from 1994 to 2001. He was a senior fellow at the [Center for Strategic and International Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Strategic_and_International_Studies "Center for Strategic and International Studies") from 2001 to 2002. He advocated for the [2003 invasion of Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq "2003 invasion of Iraq") while serving as the Democratic staff director of the [Senate Foreign Relations Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Foreign_Relations "United States Senate Committee on Foreign Relations") from 2002 to 2008.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-Joe_Biden's_Vote_for_War-2) He was a foreign policy advisor for [Joe Biden's 2008 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_2008_presidential_campaign "Joe Biden 2008 presidential campaign"), before advising the [Obama–Biden presidential transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_transition_of_Barack_Obama "Presidential transition of Barack Obama").

From 2009 to 2013, Blinken served as deputy assistant to the president and [national security advisor to the vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_the_Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Office of the Vice President of the United States"). During his tenure in the [Obama administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_administration "Obama administration"), he helped craft U.S. policy on [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan"), [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan"), and the [nuclear program of Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_program_of_Iran "Nuclear program of Iran").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-Columbia14-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-Sanger-4) After leaving government service, Blinken [moved into the private sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolving_door_(politics)#United_States "Revolving door (politics)"), co-founding [WestExec Advisors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WestExec_Advisors "WestExec Advisors"), a consulting firm. Blinken returned to government first as a foreign policy advisor for Biden's [2020 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_2020_presidential_campaign "Joe Biden 2020 presidential campaign"), then as Biden's pick for secretary of state, a position the Senate confirmed him for on January 26, 2021.

## Early life and education

Blinken was born on April 16, 1962, in [Yonkers, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonkers,_New_York "Yonkers, New York"), to [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jews "New York Jews") parents. His mother was Judith ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Née "Née") Frehm) Blinken and his father was [Donald M. Blinken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_M._Blinken "Donald M. Blinken"), a co-founder of the private equity firm [Warburg Pincus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warburg_Pincus "Warburg Pincus") who later served as the [U.S. ambassador to Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._ambassador_to_Hungary "U.S. ambassador to Hungary").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-twp-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-JVL-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-7) His maternal grandparents were Hungarian Jews.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-8) Blinken's uncle, [Alan Blinken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Blinken "Alan Blinken"), served as the [U.S. ambassador to Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_Belgium "List of ambassadors of the United States to Belgium").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-10) His grandfather, Maurice Henry Blinken, was an early backer of Israel who studied its economic viability,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-11) and his great-grandfather was [Meir Blinken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meir_Blinken "Meir Blinken"), a [Yiddish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yiddish "Yiddish") writer.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-12)

Blinken attended the [Dalton School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalton_School "Dalton School") in New York City until 1971.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-JVL-6) He then moved to Paris with his mother and [Samuel Pisar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Pisar "Samuel Pisar"); his mother married Pisar after divorcing Donald Blinken. In his confirmation hearing, Blinken recalled the story of his stepfather, Pisar, who had been the only [Holocaust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust "Holocaust") survivor of the 900 children in his school in Poland. Pisar found refuge in a U.S. tank after making a break into the forest during a [Nazi death march](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_marches_during_the_Holocaust "Death marches during the Holocaust").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-14) In Paris, Blinken attended [École Jeannine Manuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/École_Jeannine_Manuel "École Jeannine Manuel").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-15)

From 1980 to 1984, Blinken attended [Harvard College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_College "Harvard College"), where he majored in social studies. He co-edited Harvard's daily student newspaper, *[The Harvard Crimson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Harvard_Crimson "The Harvard Crimson"),*[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-twp-5)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:3-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-17) and wrote a number of articles on current affairs.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:4-19) After graduating from the university, Blinken worked as an intern for *[The New Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Republic "The New Republic")* for about a year.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-JVL-6)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:4-19) He earned a [J.D.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") from [Columbia Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Law_School "Columbia Law School") in 1988[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:2-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-21) and practiced law in New York City and Paris.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-22) Blinken worked with his father to raise funds for [Michael Dukakis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Dukakis "Michael Dukakis"), the Democratic nominee in the [1988 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_United_States_presidential_election "1988 United States presidential election").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-twp-5) He aspired for a time to be a [journalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalist "Journalist") or a [film producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_producer "Film producer").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-defender-23)

In his monograph *Ally versus Ally: America, Europe, and the Siberian Pipeline Crisis* (1987), Blinken argued that exerting diplomatic pressure on the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") during the [Siberian pipeline crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urengoy–Pomary–Uzhhorod_pipeline#Controversies "Urengoy–Pomary–Uzhhorod pipeline") was less significant for American interests than maintaining strong [relations between the United States and Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_the_United_States#Europe "Foreign relations of the United States").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-24) *Ally versus Ally* was based on Blinken's undergraduate thesis in which he interviewed [Henry Kissinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Kissinger "Henry Kissinger").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:3-16)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-25)

## Early diplomatic career (1994–2001)

Blinken has held senior foreign policy positions in two administrations over two decades.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-twp-5) He was a member of the [United States National Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_National_Security_Council "United States National Security Council") staff from 1994 to 2001.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:0-26) From 1994 to 1998, Blinken was special assistant to the president and senior director for strategic planning and National Security Council senior director for speechwriting.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-statedeptbio-27) From 1999 to 2001, he was special assistant to the president and senior director for European and Canadian affairs.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-Gallucci09-28)

## Diplomatic career

### Clinton and Bush administrations

In 2002, Blinken was appointed staff director for the [Senate Foreign Relations Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Foreign_Relations "United States Senate Committee on Foreign Relations"), a position he served in until 2008.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:0-26) Blinken assisted then-Senator Joe Biden, Chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, in formulating Biden's support for the U.S. invasion of Iraq, with Blinken characterizing the vote to invade Iraq as "a vote for tough diplomacy".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-29) Blinken supported the U.S.-led [invasion of Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_invasion_of_Iraq "2003 invasion of Iraq") in 2003.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-Joe_Biden's_Vote_for_War-2)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-30)

In the years following the U.S. invasion and occupation of Iraq, Blinken assisted Biden in formulating a proposal in the Senate to establish in Iraq three independent regions divided along ethnic or sectarian lines: a "Shiastan" in the south, a "Sunnistan" in the north, as well as [Iraqi Kurdistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Kurdistan "Iraqi Kurdistan"). The proposal was overwhelmingly rejected at home, as well as in Iraq, where the prime minister opposed the partition plan.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-defender-23)

He was also a senior fellow at the [Center for Strategic and International Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Strategic_and_International_Studies "Center for Strategic and International Studies"). In 2008, Blinken worked for [Joe Biden's presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_2008_presidential_campaign "Joe Biden 2008 presidential campaign"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-twp-5) and was a member of the [Obama–Biden presidential transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_transition_of_Barack_Obama "Presidential transition of Barack Obama") team.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-LaMonica-31)

### Obama administration

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Obama_and_Biden_await_updates_on_bin_Laden.jpg/500px-Obama_and_Biden_await_updates_on_bin_Laden.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Obama_and_Biden_await_updates_on_bin_Laden.jpg)Blinken in the [White House Situation Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Situation_Room "Situation Room") (back of the room, blue shirt, leaning) during the [Osama Bin Laden raid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_Osama_bin_Laden "Killing of Osama bin Laden"), as seen in the photograph named *[Situation Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Situation_Room_(photograph) "Situation Room (photograph)")*

From 2009 to 2013, Blinken was deputy assistant to the president and [National Security Advisor to the Vice President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Advisor_to_the_Vice_President "National Security Advisor to the Vice President"). In this position he helped craft U.S. policy on [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan"), [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan"), and the [nuclear program of Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_program_of_Iran "Nuclear program of Iran").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-Columbia14-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-Sanger-4) Blinken was sworn in as [deputy national security advisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_National_Security_Advisor "Deputy National Security Advisor"), succeeding [Denis McDonough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_McDonough "Denis McDonough"), on January 20, 2013.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-32)

On November 7, 2014, President Obama announced that he would nominate Blinken for the deputy secretary post, replacing the retiring [William J. Burns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_J._Burns_(diplomat) "William J. Burns (diplomat)").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-33) On December 16, 2014, Blinken was confirmed as Deputy Secretary of State by the Senate by a vote of 55 to 38.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-34)

Of Obama's 2011 decision to [kill Osama bin Laden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_Osama_bin_Laden "Killing of Osama bin Laden"), Blinken said "I've never seen a more courageous decision made by a leader."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-35) A 2013 profile described him as "one of the government's key players in drafting [Syria policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria–United_States_relations "Syria–United States relations")",[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-twp-5) for which he served as a public face.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-starturn-36) Blinken was influential in formulating the Obama administration's response to the [annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Federation "Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation") in the aftermath of the [2014 Ukrainian revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Ukrainian_revolution "2014 Ukrainian revolution").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-38)

Blinken supported the [2011 military intervention in Libya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_military_intervention_in_Libya "2011 military intervention in Libya")[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-starturn-36) and the [supply of weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timber_Sycamore "Timber Sycamore") to [Syrian rebels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_opposition "Syrian opposition").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-39) He condemned the [2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Turkish_coup_d'état_attempt "2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt") and expressed support for the democratically elected Turkish government and its institutions, but also criticized the [2016–present purges in Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016–present_purges_in_Turkey "2016–present purges in Turkey").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-dw2020-40) In April 2015, Blinken voiced support for the [Saudi Arabian–led intervention in Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabian–led_intervention_in_Yemen "Saudi Arabian–led intervention in Yemen").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-41) He said that "as part of that effort, we have expedited weapons deliveries, we have increased our intelligence sharing, and we have established a joint coordination planning cell in the Saudi operation centre."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-42)

Blinken worked with Biden on requests for American money to replenish Israel's arsenal of [Iron Dome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Dome "Iron Dome") interceptor missiles during the [2014 Israel–Gaza conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Israel–Gaza_conflict "2014 Israel–Gaza conflict").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-43) In May 2015, Blinken criticized the [persecution of Muslims in Myanmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persecution_of_Muslims_in_Myanmar "Persecution of Muslims in Myanmar") and warned Myanmar's leaders about the dangers of anti-Muslim legislation,[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-44) saying that [Rohingya Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohingya_people "Rohingya people") "should have a path to citizenship. The uncertainty that comes from not having any status is one of the things that may drive people to leave."[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-45)

In June 2015, Blinken claimed that more than ten thousand ISIL fighters had been killed by American-led airstrikes against the [Islamic State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Iraq_and_the_Levant "Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant") since a U.S.-led coalition launched a [campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_military_intervention_against_ISIL "International military intervention against ISIL") against it nine months previously.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-46)

## U.S. Secretary of State (2021–2025)

Main article: [Foreign policy of the Biden administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_policy_of_the_Biden_administration "Foreign policy of the Biden administration")

### Nomination and confirmation

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/Secretary_Blinken_is_Sworn_in_as_Secretary_of_State_%2850878397918%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Blinken_is_Sworn_in_as_Secretary_of_State_%2850878397918%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Blinken_is_Sworn_in_as_Secretary_of_State_(50878397918).jpg)Blinken being sworn in as [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State") at the [U.S. State Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State") on January 26, 2021

Blinken was a [foreign policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_policy_of_the_United_States "Foreign policy of the United States") advisor for Biden's [2020 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_2020_presidential_campaign "Joe Biden 2020 presidential campaign").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-47) On November 22, 2020, [Bloomberg News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_News "Bloomberg News") reported that Biden had selected Blinken as his nominee for secretary of state.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-longtimeaide-48) These reports were later corroborated by *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* and other outlets.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-defender-23)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-49) On November 24, upon being announced as Biden's choice for secretary of state, Blinken said, "We can't solve all the world's problems alone [and] we need to be working with other countries."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-50) He had earlier remarked in a September 2020 interview with the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") that "democracy is in retreat around the world, and unfortunately it's also in retreat at home because of the president taking a two-by-four to its institutions, its values and its people every day."[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-51)

Blinken's confirmation hearing before the [Senate Foreign Relations Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Foreign_Relations "United States Senate Committee on Foreign Relations") began on January 19, 2021. His nomination was confirmed by the committee on January 25 with a vote of 15–3.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-52) On January 26, Blinken was confirmed in the full Senate by a vote of 78–22.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-auto-1) Blinken took the oath of office of the secretary of state later that day.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-53) In doing so, he became the third former deputy secretary of state to serve as the [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State"), after [Lawrence Eagleburger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Eagleburger "Lawrence Eagleburger") and [Warren Christopher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Christopher "Warren Christopher") in 1992 and 1993, respectively.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-55)

### Tenure

See also: [List of international trips made by Antony Blinken as United States Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_trips_made_by_Antony_Blinken_as_United_States_Secretary_of_State "List of international trips made by Antony Blinken as United States Secretary of State")

#### Africa

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Secretary_Blinken_Meets_With_Kenyan_President_Ruto_%2852375711450%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Blinken_Meets_With_Kenyan_President_Ruto_%2852375711450%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Blinken_Meets_With_Kenyan_President_Ruto_(52375711450).jpg)Blinken meeting with Kenyan President [William Ruto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Ruto "William Ruto") on September 21, 2022

In February 2021, Blinken condemned [ethnic cleansing in the Tigray region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_crimes_in_the_Tigray_War "War crimes in the Tigray War") of northern [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia") and called for the immediate withdrawal of [Eritrean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrean_Defence_Forces "Eritrean Defence Forces") forces and other fighters.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-57)

In the midst of the Biden administration's continuing review of the [normalization agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel–Morocco_normalization_agreement "Israel–Morocco normalization agreement") between Morocco and Israel enacted during the previous administration, Blinken maintained that the recognition of [Morocco's sovereignty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_status_of_Western_Sahara "Political status of Western Sahara") over the [disputed territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_dispute "Territorial dispute") of [Western Sahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Sahara "Western Sahara"), which was annexed by Morocco in 1975, will not be reversed imminently. During internal discussions, he supported improving relations between the two countries and expressed urgency in appointing a United Nations envoy to Western Sahara.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-59)

In March 2023, Blinken met with Ethiopian prime minister [Abiy Ahmed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abiy_Ahmed "Abiy Ahmed") in Addis Ababa to normalize relations between the United States and [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia") that were strained by the [Tigray War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_War "Tigray War") between the Ethiopian government and [Tigray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigray_Region "Tigray Region") rebels.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-60)

In January 2025, Blinken declared that the combatants in the [Sudanese civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudanese_civil_war_(2023–present) "Sudanese civil war (2023–present)") were carrying out a [genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darfur_genocide_(2023–present) "Darfur genocide (2023–present)").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-nyt-20250118-61)

#### Asia

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Tony_Blinken_and_Bongbong_Marcos_shaking_hands_2_%282022-08-06%29.jpg/250px-Tony_Blinken_and_Bongbong_Marcos_shaking_hands_2_%282022-08-06%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tony_Blinken_and_Bongbong_Marcos_shaking_hands_2_(2022-08-06).jpg)Blinken with Philippine President [Bongbong Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos "Bongbong Marcos") in [Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila "Manila") on August 6, 2022

Blinken made his first international trip with Secretary of Defense [Lloyd Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Austin "Lloyd Austin") to [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo") and [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul") on March 15, during which he warned [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") against coercion and aggression.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-63) He also condemned the Chinese government for committing [genocide against ethnic Uyghurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persecution_of_Uyghurs_in_China "Persecution of Uyghurs in China").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-64)

In July 2021, the Biden administration accused China of a [global cyberespionage campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_intelligence_activity_abroad "Chinese intelligence activity abroad"), which Blinken said posed "a major threat to our economic and national security".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-65)

In late April 2021, Blinken denounced the sentencing of Hong Kong pro-democracy activists [Jimmy Lai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Lai "Jimmy Lai"), [Albert Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Ho "Albert Ho"), and [Lee Cheuk-yan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Cheuk-yan "Lee Cheuk-yan") among others, for their roles in the [2019 Hong Kong protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019–2020_Hong_Kong_protests "2019–2020 Hong Kong protests"), calling it a "politically-motivated" decision.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-67)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/Secretary_Blinken_Meets_with_Chinese_State_Councilor_and_Foreign_Minister_Wang_Yi_in_Bali_%2852204013285%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Blinken_Meets_with_Chinese_State_Councilor_and_Foreign_Minister_Wang_Yi_in_Bali_%2852204013285%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Blinken_Meets_with_Chinese_State_Councilor_and_Foreign_Minister_Wang_Yi_in_Bali_(52204013285).jpg)Secretary of State Antony J. Blinken meets with Chinese State Councilor and Foreign Minister [Wang Yi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Yi_(politician) "Wang Yi (politician)") in [Bali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bali "Bali"), [Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia"), on July 9, 2022.

In May 2022, Blinken stated that "China is the one country that has the intention as well as the economic, technological, military and diplomatic means to advance a different vision of international order."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-68) He dismissed China's claims to be neutral in the [Russo-Ukrainian War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_War "Russo-Ukrainian War") and accused China of supporting [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-69)

In May 2022, Blinken says U.S. to rely on "Alliances", "Trade" and "Investment" to [counter China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_foreign_policy_toward_the_People's_Republic_of_China "United States foreign policy toward the People's Republic of China"), and focus on defending the rules-based order Beijing is trying to reshape.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-70)

In June 2023, Blinken met with Chinese president [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping") during his trip to Beijing. According to the State Department's readout, Blinken "emphasized the importance of maintaining open channels of communication across the full range of issues to reduce the risk of miscalculation" and "made clear that while we will compete vigorously, the United States will responsibly manage that competition so that the relationship does not veer into conflict."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-71)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/P20231115AS-1223.jpg/250px-P20231115AS-1223.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:P20231115AS-1223.jpg)Biden and Blinken meet Xi and Yi at the [2023 Woodside Summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Woodside_Summit "2023 Woodside Summit").

On November 15, 2023, Blinken accompanied Biden as together they hosted [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping") and [Wang Yi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Yi_(politician) "Wang Yi (politician)") in [Woodside, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodside,_California "Woodside, California") and the so-called [2023 Woodside Summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Woodside_Summit "2023 Woodside Summit"). Top-level cabinet officials, such as [Janet Yellen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Yellen "Janet Yellen") and [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry") also were at the meeting table there.

#### Myanmar

On January 31, 2021, Blinken condemned the [2021 Myanmar coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Myanmar_coup_d'état "2021 Myanmar coup d'état") and expressed grave concerns on the detention of government officials and civil society leaders, calling for their immediate release.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-72) He stated that, "the United States will continue to take firm action against those who perpetrate violence against the people of Burma as they demand the restoration of their democratically elected government."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-73)

#### Afghanistan

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Secretary_Blinken_Meets_with_Afghan_President_Ghani_%2851126100940%29.jpg/250px-Secretary_Blinken_Meets_with_Afghan_President_Ghani_%2851126100940%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Blinken_Meets_with_Afghan_President_Ghani_(51126100940).jpg)Blinken meeting with Afghan president [Ashraf Ghani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashraf_Ghani "Ashraf Ghani") to discuss [U.S. troop withdrawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Withdrawal_of_United_States_troops_from_Afghanistan_(2020–2021) "Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)")

In February 2021, having spoken to president [Ashraf Ghani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashraf_Ghani "Ashraf Ghani"), Blinken voiced support for [Afghan peace negotiations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_peace_process "Afghan peace process") with [Taliban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban "Taliban") [Islamist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamism "Islamism") rebels and reiterated the United States' commitment to a peace deal that includes a "just and durable political settlement and permanent and comprehensive ceasefire."[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-74)

Blinken made an unannounced visit to [Kabul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul "Kabul") on April 15 and met with U.S. military and diplomatic personnel following the Biden administration's announcement of the [2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_withdrawal_of_U.S._troops_from_Afghanistan "2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-75) He said the decision to withdraw from [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan") was made to focus resources on China and the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-76) He faced calls to resign as secretary of state following the US withdrawal from Afghanistan.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-80)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/C-17_carrying_passengers_out_of_Afghanistan.jpg/250px-C-17_carrying_passengers_out_of_Afghanistan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:C-17_carrying_passengers_out_of_Afghanistan.jpg)A USAF C-17 evacuating 823 fleeing Afghan citizens from [Kabul Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul_Airport "Kabul Airport") on August 15, 2021

In August 2021, Blinken rejected comparisons between the deteriorating situation in Afghanistan due to the [Taliban offensive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Taliban_offensive "2021 Taliban offensive"), which started in May 2021 after U.S. and coalition military forces began withdrawing from Afghanistan, and the chaotic [American departure from Saigon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_Saigon "Fall of Saigon") in 1975, saying that "We went to Afghanistan 20 years ago with one mission, and that mission was to deal with the folks who attacked us on [9/11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks") and we have succeeded in that mission."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-81)

On September 25, 2024, the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") passed a resolution condemning the Biden-Harris administration for the U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan. The resolution passed 219-194, with 10 Democrats and all Republicans voting in favor.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-82) Two *[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Times "New York Times")* diplomatic correspondents in a 2025 end of term assessment called the withdrawal Blinken's first test as Secretary of State, stating it was widely considered a fiasco.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-nyt-20250118-61)

#### Israel–Palestine

During the [2021 Israeli-Palestinian conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Israel–Palestine_crisis "2021 Israel–Palestine crisis"), Blinken expressed "absolute" support for [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel")'s right to defend itself but warned that evicting Palestinian families from their homes in [East Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Jerusalem "East Jerusalem") is among the actions that could further escalate outbreaks of violence and retaliation.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:1-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:5-84) He, along with the [United Nations Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council"), called for full adherence to the truce and stressed the immediate need for humanitarian aid for Palestinian civilians while reiterating the need for a [two-state solution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-state_solution "Two-state solution").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-85) Following a ceasefire and coinciding Blinken's visit to Jerusalem on May 25, the transfer of food and medical supplies furnished by the United Nations and [Physicians for Human Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physicians_for_Human_Rights "Physicians for Human Rights"), aid workers, and journalists were permitted into the Gaza Strip.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-86)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Secretary_Blinken_Meets_with_Israeli_War_Cabinet_-_53453976243.jpg/250px-Secretary_Blinken_Meets_with_Israeli_War_Cabinet_-_53453976243.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Secretary_Blinken_Meets_with_Israeli_War_Cabinet_-_53453976243.jpg)Ministers of the [Israeli war cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_war_cabinet "Israeli war cabinet") meeting with Blinken, January 9, 2024

During a visit to Tel Aviv following the [October 7 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks "October 7 attacks"), Blinken promised to help defend Israel "as long as America exists." Blinken said that "Israel has the right, indeed the obligation, to defend itself and to ensure that this never happens again."[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:6-87) He rejected calls for a ceasefire in the [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war") but said he supported "humanitarian pauses" to deliver aid to the people of the [Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:7-88) Blinken allegedly participated in Netanyahu's cabinet policy decisions on humanitarian aid, which allowed the targeting of aid convoys that could reach [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas"). Implementation of the policy resulted in assaults on [UNRWA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNRWA "UNRWA") aid trucks, Palestinian police escorts for aid convoys, the [World Central Kitchen aid convoy attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Central_Kitchen_aid_convoy_attack "World Central Kitchen aid convoy attack"), and the assassination of [Anera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anera "Anera") aid workers.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-89)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/United_States_Secretary_of_State_Antony_Blinken_visits_Israel_on_October_22%2C_2024_-_26.jpg/250px-United_States_Secretary_of_State_Antony_Blinken_visits_Israel_on_October_22%2C_2024_-_26.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:United_States_Secretary_of_State_Antony_Blinken_visits_Israel_on_October_22,_2024_-_26.jpg)Blinken with Israeli prime minister [Benjamin Netanyahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu"), October 22, 2024

In April 2024, it was reported that Blinken had refused to act on recommendations from the [Israel Leahy Vetting Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leahy_Law "Leahy Law") to sanction Israeli units that had been accused of human rights violations including torture, rape, and extrajudicial killings in the [West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank "West Bank").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-91) During a hearing before the [Senate Foreign Relations Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Foreign_Relations_Committee "Senate Foreign Relations Committee") on May 21, 2024, Blinken faced fierce criticism from protestors who interrupted his testimony by shouting as they were escorted from the hearing room, including calling him "the Butcher of Gaza" and "Bloody Blinken".[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-93) A *[Times of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Times_of_Israel "The Times of Israel")* report found that in August 2024, Blinken falsely announced that [Benjamin Netanyahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu") had accepted a US proposal for a hostage deal, which [threw a wrench in the works](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/threw%20a%20wrench%20in%20the%20works "wikt:threw a wrench in the works") and lead to the round of negotiations falling apart.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-94)

[ProPublica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ProPublica "ProPublica") reported on September 24, 2024, that Blinken lied to the U.S. Congress, ignoring two reports, one from the [U.S. Agency for International Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Agency_for_International_Development "U.S. Agency for International Development") (USAID), the other from State Department [Refugees Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Population,_Refugees,_and_Migration "Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration"), that Israel had indeed [blocked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blocking_of_humanitarian_aid "Blocking of humanitarian aid") [humanitarian aid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanitarian_aid_during_the_Gaza_war "Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war") from reaching Gaza.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-ProPublica-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-96) First-hand reports had previously shown Israelis [blocking and even destroying aid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_blockade_of_aid_delivery_to_the_Gaza_Strip "Israeli blockade of aid delivery to the Gaza Strip") on trucks.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-98)
> "Their conclusion was explosive because U.S. law requires the government to cut off weapons shipments to countries that prevent the delivery of U.S.-backed humanitarian aid. Israel has been largely dependent on American bombs and other weapons in Gaza since Hamas’ Oct. 7 attacks."[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-ProPublica-95)

Following the report, [U.S. representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._representative "U.S. representative") [Rashida Tlaib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashida_Tlaib "Rashida Tlaib")[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-99) and the [Council on American–Islamic Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_on_American–Islamic_Relations "Council on American–Islamic Relations") called for Blinken's resignation.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-100)

On January 14, 2025, Blinken expressed his assessment that Hamas had recruited almost as many new members as it had lost in the Israel–Hamas war and that this was due to Benjamin Netanyahu's refusal to advance an alternative to Hamas leadership in Gaza.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-101) In that same speech, Blinken was interrupted by three protesters who reiterated the common sobriquet "Bloody Blinken" and referred to him as the "Secretary of [Genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_genocide "Gaza genocide")".[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-102)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-103) During his final press conference as Secretary of State, journalists [Max Blumenthal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Blumenthal "Max Blumenthal") and [Sam Husseini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Husseini "Sam Husseini") were forcefully removed after asking questions about Gaza policy.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-105)

#### Russia-Ukraine war

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/%D0%97%D1%83%D1%81%D1%82%D1%80%D1%96%D1%87_%D0%9F%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%B8%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B0_%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%97%D0%BD%D0%B8_%D0%B7_%D0%94%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B6%D0%B0%D0%B2%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%BC_%D1%81%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%82%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC_%D0%A1%D0%A8%D0%90_21.jpg/250px-%D0%97%D1%83%D1%81%D1%82%D1%80%D1%96%D1%87_%D0%9F%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%B8%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%82%D0%B0_%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%97%D0%BD%D0%B8_%D0%B7_%D0%94%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B6%D0%B0%D0%B2%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%BC_%D1%81%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%82%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC_%D0%A1%D0%A8%D0%90_21.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Зустріч_Президента_України_з_Державним_секретарем_США_21.jpg)Blinken meets with Ukrainian president [Volodymyr Zelenskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "Volodymyr Zelenskyy") in Kyiv in 2022. As Secretary of State, Blinken has been deeply involved in the American response to the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine").

During heightened Russia-Ukraine [tensions in 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prelude_to_the_2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine"), Blinken attended a meeting with President [Volodymyr Zelenskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "Volodymyr Zelenskyy") and foreign minister [Dmytro Kuleba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmytro_Kuleba "Dmytro Kuleba") in [Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv "Kyiv"), where Blinken reaffirmed support for [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine")'s sovereignty and territorial integrity against "Russian aggression".[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-113)

In January 2022, Blinken authorized the [supply of weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_military_aid "United States military aid") to [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") to support the Eastern European country in amid border tensions with Russia.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-115) At a joint press availability with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba on January 19, Blinken said "One of the principles which you've heard us repeat – but it always bears repeating – is [nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nothing_about_Ukraine_without_Ukraine "Nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-116) Blinken publicly warned on February 11 of the likelihood of a [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021–2022_Russo-Ukrainian_crisis "2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis") prior to the end the [2022 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Winter_Olympics "2022 Winter Olympics")[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-117) and on February 13, he said the risk was "high enough and the threat is imminent enough" that the [evacuation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_evacuation "Emergency evacuation") of most staff from the U.S. Embassy in [Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv "Kyiv") was "the prudent thing to do".[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-118) In September 2022, Blinken pledged that the United States would help the Ukrainian military retake [Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian-occupied_territories_of_Ukraine "Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-119) He criticized [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin")'s threats to use [nuclear weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapons "Nuclear weapons"), saying that "Russia has gotten itself into the mess that it's in is because there is no one in the [autocratic] system to effectively tell Putin he's doing the wrong thing."[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-120)

Regarding the countries that decided to be [neutral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutral_country "Neutral country") in the war between Russia and Ukraine, Blinken said that "It's pretty hard to be neutral when it comes to this aggression. There is a clear aggressor. There is a clear victim."[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-121)

Speaking about the [2022 Russian mobilization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_mobilization "2022 Russian mobilization"), he said that mobilized Russian civilians were being treated as "cannon fodder that Putin is trying to throw into the war."[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-122) On October 21, 2022, Blinken said the United States saw no willingness on the side of Russia to end its war in Ukraine by [diplomatic means](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russia–Ukraine_peace_negotiations "2022 Russia–Ukraine peace negotiations"), despite American attempts.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-123) In late 2022, the US Joint Chiefs of Staff [Mark Milley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Milley "Mark Milley") suggested that Ukraine should take advantage of battlefield gains [in Kharkiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Kharkiv_counteroffensive "2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive") and [Kherson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Kherson_counteroffensive "2022 Kherson counteroffensive") to seek peace talks, however Blinken rejected this advice.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-nyt-20250118-61) Blinken questioned China's [peace proposal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_during_the_Russo-Ukrainian_War#Peace_proposal "China during the Russo-Ukrainian War"), saying "the world should not be fooled by any tactical move by Russia, supported by China or any other country, to freeze the war on its own terms."[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-124) In June 2023, he rejected any "cease-fire that simply freezes current lines in place".[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-125) In July 2023, he defended Biden's decision to supply Ukraine with [cluster munitions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cluster_munition "Cluster munition").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-126) In June 2024, Blinken said that [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China")'s support for Russia was prolonging the war in Ukraine.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-127)

#### South America

In 2021, Blinken spoke with the [interim president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuelan_presidential_crisis "Venezuelan presidential crisis") of [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela"), [Juan Guaidó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Guaidó "Juan Guaidó"), whom the Biden administration continued to recognize as the country's head of state and not [Nicolás Maduro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolás_Maduro "Nicolás Maduro").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-128)

#### Americans detained abroad

Blinken and the Biden administration have been criticized for the handling of [Americans who are wrongfully imprisoned abroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Americans_wrongfully_imprisoned_or_detained_abroad "List of Americans wrongfully imprisoned or detained abroad"). Families of U.S. detainees in the Middle East were upset that they were left off of a call with Secretary Blinken.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-129) In July 2022, Blinken had a meeting with [Sergey Lavrov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergey_Lavrov "Sergey Lavrov") to discuss a prisoner swap to secure the release of [Paul Whelan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Whelan "Paul Whelan") and [Brittney Griner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brittney_Griner "Brittney Griner").[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-130) Blinken has met with the [Bring Our Families Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bring_Our_Families_Home "Bring Our Families Home") campaign, a coalition of families with loved ones detained abroad.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-131)

Blinken, along with the work of Special Presidential Envoy of Hostage Affairs [Roger D. Carstens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_D._Carstens "Roger D. Carstens"), has negotiated the release of over a dozen Americans wrongfully detained or held hostage abroad including [Trevor Reed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Reed "Trevor Reed"), [Danny Fenster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Fenster "Danny Fenster"), [Baquer Namazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baquer_Namazi "Baquer Namazi"), the entire [Citgo Six](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citgo_Six "Citgo Six"), Osman Khan, [Matthew John Heath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_John_Heath "Matthew John Heath"), [Mark Frerichs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Frerichs "Mark Frerichs"), and Jorge Alberto Fernández.[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

#### Contempt of Congress

On September 24, 2024, the [House Foreign Affairs Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Foreign_Affairs_Committee "House Foreign Affairs Committee") voted to recommend Blinken be held in [contempt of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contempt_of_Congress "Contempt of Congress") for failing to comply with a subpoena seeking information about the 2021 U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-132) [Speaker of the House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speaker_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives "Speaker of the United States House of Representatives") [Mike Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Johnson "Mike Johnson") commented that he expected the measure would likely not be taken up for a vote until after the 2024 presidential election, although a vote was never held.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-133)

## Post-Biden administration (2025–present)

On January 28, 2025, [Crown Publishing Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_Publishing_Group "Crown Publishing Group") announced that Blinken had agreed to write a book on his experiences as Secretary of State.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-134)

On February 8, 2025, [President Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_Trump "President Trump") stated that he would be stripping Blinken's security clearance in an interview with the *New York Post*.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-135) The decision was later confirmed, with Trump ordering the removal of Blinken’s access to classified information. Trump also announced plans to revoke the security clearances of several other officials, including former president Joe Biden, [Letitia James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letitia_James "Letitia James"), [Alvin Bragg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvin_Bragg "Alvin Bragg"), and former national security adviser [Jake Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Sullivan "Jake Sullivan").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-136)

On April 9, 2025, Blinken was interviewed by [Andrew Ross Sorkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Ross_Sorkin "Andrew Ross Sorkin") about the [Tariffs in the second Trump administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariffs_in_the_second_Trump_administration "Tariffs in the second Trump administration"), as well as other foreign policy matters.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-137)
