## Other activities

### Film producing

During the 1990s, Blinken was briefly involved in film producing. He was an associate producer on the 1995 film *[The Addiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Addiction "The Addiction")*, directed by [Abel Ferrara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Ferrara "Abel Ferrara").[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-167)

### WestExec Advisors

In 2017, Blinken co-founded [WestExec Advisors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WestExec_Advisors "WestExec Advisors"), a political strategy advising firm, with [Michèle Flournoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michèle_Flournoy "Michèle Flournoy"), Sergio Aguirre, and Nitin Chadda.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-168)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-169) WestExec's clients have included Google's [Jigsaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jigsaw_(company) "Jigsaw (company)"), Israeli artificial-intelligence company Windward, surveillance drone manufacturer Shield AI, which signed a $7.2 million contract with the Air Force,[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-nyt20201128-170) and "*Fortune* 100 types".[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-171) According to *[Foreign Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Policy "Foreign Policy")*, the firm's clientele includes "the defense industry, private equity firms, and hedge funds".[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-172) Blinken received almost $1.2 million in compensation from WestExec.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-173)

In an interview with *[The Intercept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Intercept "The Intercept")*, Flournoy described WestExec's role as facilitating relationships between [Silicon Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon_Valley "Silicon Valley") firms and the [Department of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense "United States Department of Defense") and law enforcement;[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-FangIntercept-174) Flournoy and others compared WestExec to [Kissinger Associates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kissinger_Associates "Kissinger Associates").[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-FangIntercept-174)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-175)

### Pine Island Capital Partners

Blinken, as well as other Biden transition team members [Michele Flournoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Flournoy "Michele Flournoy"), former Pentagon advisor, and [Lloyd Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Austin "Lloyd Austin"), Secretary of Defense, are partners of [private equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_equity "Private equity") firm Pine Island Capital Partners,[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-176)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-dailybeast20201208-177) a strategic partner of WestExec.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-common-178) Pine Island's chairman is [John Thain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Thain "John Thain"), the final chairman of [Merrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merrill_(company) "Merrill (company)") before its sale to [Bank of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_America "Bank of America").[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-179) Blinken went on leave from Pine Island in August 2020 to join the Biden campaign as a senior foreign policy advisor.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-dailybeast20201208-177) He said he would divest himself of his equity stake in Pine Island if confirmed for a position in the Biden administration.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-common-178)

During the final stretch of Biden's presidential campaign, Pine Island raised $218 million for a [special-purpose acquisition company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special-purpose_acquisition_company "Special-purpose acquisition company"), a public offering to invest in "defense, government service and aerospace industries" and [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") relief, which the firm's prospectus (initially filed with the U.S. SEC in September and finalized on November 13, 2020) predicted would be profitable as the government looked to private contractors to address the pandemic.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-dailybeast20201208-177) Thain said he chose the other partners because of their "access, network and expertise".[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-nyt20201128-170)

In a December 2020 *[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Times "New York Times")* article raising questions about potential conflicts of interest between WestExec principals, Pine Island advisors, including Blinken, and service in the Biden administration, critics called for full disclosure of all WestExec/Pine Island financial relationships, divestiture of ownership stakes in companies bidding on government contracts or enjoying existing contracts, and assurances that Blinken and others recuse themselves from decisions that might advantage their previous clients.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-nyt20201128-170)

Blinken is a member of the [Council on Foreign Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_on_Foreign_Relations "Council on Foreign Relations")[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-180) and was previously a global affairs analyst for [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN").[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-181)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-182)

### Penn Biden Center

From 2017 to 2019, Blinken served as the managing director of the [Penn Biden Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penn_Biden_Center "Penn Biden Center"), a [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania") think tank based in Washington.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-183) During this time he published several articles on foreign policy and the [Trump administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "First presidency of Donald Trump").

## Public image

In general, Blinken is widely seen as a close protégé of Joe Biden and a key part of the Biden administration’s legacy. He has received praise for his role in attempting to strengthen the United States’ international partnerships, particularly with Europe and NATO allies.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-184)

Blinken has faced criticism for elements of foreign policy enacted during the [Biden presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Joe_Biden "Presidency of Joe Biden"), particularly the [Afghanistan withdrawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020–2021_U.S._troop_withdrawal_from_Afghanistan "2020–2021 U.S. troop withdrawal from Afghanistan"), the lead-up to the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), and Israel’s [assault on Gaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_genocide "Gaza genocide") in response to the [October 7 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks "October 7 attacks").[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:8-185) Critics and detractors of Blinken have pointed to the Biden administration’s support for Israeli policy in Gaza as a violation of human rights, given that Israeli Prime Minister [Benjamin Netanyahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu") is the subject of an [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") warrant and the [International Court of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice "International Court of Justice") is investigating his government for "[plausible genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa's_genocide_case_against_Israel "South Africa's genocide case against Israel")."[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-186)[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-187) Blinken considered working with Congress to sanction the ICC in response to these arrest warrants.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-188) [[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-190)

Some State Department employees resigned in protest during Blinken’s tenure, citing the emotional burden of working under him. One official stated: “I got so tired of writing about dead kids.... Just constantly having to prove to Washington that these children actually died and then watching nothing happen.”[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-191)

Activists have referred to him as “Bloody Blinken,” “The Butcher of Gaza,” and “The Secretary of Genocide,”[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-192)[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-193) and took the step of setting up a permanent protest camp outside his Northern Virginia home.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-194)

When asked directly in January 2025 if he worried that he had presided over what the world would see as a genocide, Blinken responded: “No. It’s not, first of all. Second, as to how the world sees it, I can’t fully answer to that. But everyone has to look at the facts and draw their own conclusions from those facts.”[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-:8-185) Subsequently, the [International Association of Genocide Scholars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Association_of_Genocide_Scholars "International Association of Genocide Scholars")[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-195) and a [UN commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_International_Commission_of_Inquiry_on_the_Occupied_Palestinian_Territory "Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory")[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-196)[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-197) both resolved that the assault on Gaza did indeed meet the [legal definition of genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_definition_of_genocide "Legal definition of genocide").

In public opinion polling, 26% of respondents reported a favorable or very favorable opinion of Blinken, 31% had a somewhat or very unfavorable opinion, and 44% had no opinion at all in a poll conducted in December 2023.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antony_Blinken#cite_note-198)

resposta:
## Relatório das 82ª Premiações do Golden Globe (2025)

**Data:** 5 de janeiro de 2025  
**Local:** The Beverly Hilton, Beverly Hills, Califórnia, EUA  
**Anfitriã:** Nikki Glaser – primeira mulher a apresentar sozinha na história do evento  
**Transmissão:** CBS e streaming no Paramount+  

---

### 1. Prêmios de Cinema (Motion Pictures)

| Categoria | Vencedora | Distribuidor / Plataforma |
|-----------|-----------|----------------------------|
| Melhor Filme – Drama | **The Brutalist** | A24 |
| Melhor Filme – Musical ou Comédia | **Emilia Pérez** | Netflix |
| Melhor Filme – Animado | **Flow** | Sideshow / Janus Films |
| Melhor Filme – Não em Inglês | **Emilia Pérez** | Netflix |
| Melhor Ator – Drama | **Adrien Brody** (*The Brutalist*) | — |
| Melhor Atriz – Drama | **Fernanda Torres** (*I’m Still Here*) | — |
| Melhor Ator – Musical/Comédia | **Sebastian Stan** (*A Different Man*) | — |
| Melhor Atriz – Musical/Comédia | **Demi Moore** (*The Substance*) | — |
| Melhor Ator de Apoio – Filme | **Kieran Culkin** (*A Real Pain*) | Searchlight Pictures |
| Melhor Atriz de Apoio – Filme | **Zoe Saldaña** (*Emilia Pérez*) | — |
| Diretor – Filme | **Brady Corbet** (*The Brutalist*) | — |
| Roteiro – Filme | **Peter Straughan** (*Conclave*) / **Jacques Audiard** (*Emilia Pérez*) | — |
| Trilha Sonora – Filme | **Trent Reznor & Atticus Ross** (*Challengers*) | — |
| Canção Original – Filme | **“El Mal”** (*Emilia Pérez*) | — |
| Reconhecimento Cinematográfico e Box‑Office | **Wicked** | Universal Pictures |

---

### 2. Prêmios de Televisão

| Categoria | Vencedora | Rede / Plataforma |
|-----------|-----------|-------------------|
| Melhor Série de Televisão – Drama | **Shōgun** | FX / Hulu |
| Melhor Atriz – Série de Televisão – Drama | **Anna Sawai** (*Shōgun*) | FX / Hulu |
| Melhor Ator – Série de Televisão – Drama | **Hiroyuki Sanada** (*Shōgun*) | FX / Hulu |
| Melhor Série de Televisão – Musical/Comédia | **Hacks** | HBO / Max |
| Melhor Atriz – Série de Televisão – Musical/Comédia | **Jean Smart** (*Hacks*) | HBO / Max |
| Melhor Ator – Série de Televisão – Musical/Comédia | **Jeremy Allen White** (*The Bear*) | FX / Hulu |
| Melhor Série Limitada / Anthology / TV Movie | **Baby Reindeer** | Netflix |
| Melhor Ator – Série Limitada / Anthology / TV Movie | **Colin Farrell** (*The Penguin*) | HBO / Max |
| Melhor Atriz – Série Limitada / Anthology / TV Movie | **Jodie Foster** (*True Detective: Night Country*) | HBO / Max |
| Performance Especial de Comédia de Stand‑up na TV | **Ali Wong** (*Ali Wong: Single Lady*) | Netflix |
| Outras categorias de performance individual (ver tabela acima) | — | — |

---

### 3. Produções com **múltiplas vitórias** (mais de um prêmio na noite)

| Produto | Número de Vitórias | Categorias Vencidas |
|---------|--------------------|---------------------|
| **Emilia Pérez** | **4** | Filme – Musical/Comédia, Filme – Não em Inglês, Atriz Musical/Comédia, etc. |
| **Shōgun** | **4** | Série – Drama, Ator Principal – Drama, Atriz Principal – Drama, etc. |
| **The Brutalist** | **3** | Filme – Drama, Diretor, etc. |
| **Baby Reindeer** | **2** | Série Limitada/Anthology e outra categoria |
| **Hacks** | **2** | Série – Musical/Comédia e outra categoria |

> **Nota:** Emilia Pérez e Shōgun foram as maiores vítimas do dia, cada uma com quatro vitórias. O filme *The Brutalist* seguiu com três vitórias. As séries *Baby Reindeer* e *Hacks* conquistaram duas vitórias cada.

---

### 4. Outros destaques

- **Emilia Pérez** também foi a primeira produção não‑em inglês a ganhar o prêmio de Melhor Filme – Musical/Comédia.  
- **Flow**, uma animação latviana, foi a primeira a vencer o prêmio de Melhor Filme – Animado.  
- **Wicked** recebeu o prêmio de Reconhecimento Cinematográfico e Box‑Office.  
- **Ali Wong** venceu o prêmio de Melhor Performance em Comédia de Stand‑up na televisão.  
- **Viola Davis** e **Ted Danson** receberam os prêmios Honorários Cecil B. DeMille e Carol Burnett durante a gala pré‑telecast.

---

### 5. Conclusão

A noite da 82ª edição do Golden Globe foi marcada por grandes vitórias de **Emilia Pérez** e **Shōgun**, com **The Brutalist** liderando nas categorias de cinema e **Baby Reindeer** e **Hacks** conquistando duas prêmios cada. O total de prêmios distribuído entre filmes e séries foi impressionante, destacando a predominância de produções internacionais e de séries de longa duração.

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)
